key_insight: HTP-Net combines edge-preserving downsampling, global topology modeling, and orientation-aware instance segmentation to count dense welding stubs more accurately.
engineering_relevance: The method supports factory-floor metrology and inventory management by improving detection, boundary precision, and robust counting of slender overlapping welding materials.
method: Wavelet-Driven Edge-Preserving module retains fine boundaries during downsampling.
Long-Range Topology Representation Block preserves connectivity for slender, disconnected-looking targets.
Orientation-Driven Instance Segmentation head reduces NMS errors and overlapping mask artifacts using rotation priors.
evidence_signal: Across custom and public dense-slender-target datasets, the method improves mAP50 by at least 1.2% and up to 55.3%, and the deployed system reports 99% accuracy for electrodes and 94% for wire stubs.
watch_item: Real-world deployment may depend on careful calibration to local lighting, occlusion, and product-shape variation in factory environments.
paper_title: High-resolution topology-preserving instance segmentation network for vision-based measurement system of dense welding material stubs
